title: Kentucky August 2026 ex parte renewal share
question: Kentucky's ex parte renewal share for August 2026, from the original (O) submission in CMS State Medicaid and CHIP Eligibility Processing Data, first official publication, rounded to one decimal.
resolutionSource: CMS, State Medicaid and CHIP Eligibility Processing Data (data.medicaid.gov)
resolutionRule: Resolves to Kentucky's ex parte renewal share for the August 2026 reporting period, computed from the original (O) submission row in CMS dataset 5abea2e0-3f8e-4b49-a50d-d63d5fd9103c when CMS first publishes it (expected roughly three to four months after the period). Numerator and denominator as published; share computed to one decimal.

reasoning.text: The initial official API fetch succeeded and exposed Kentucky original-submission history. No local files or prohibited forecast sources were accessed.

reasoning.call: Fetch Kentucky rows from CMS dataset 5abea2e0-3f8e-4b49-a50d-d63d5fd9103c through its datastore API; read the echoed JSON response.

reasoning.text: A subsequent request intended to narrow the successful history response returned status 400 with 'JSON Schema validation failed.' Following the instruction to stop after a failed fetch, no retry or further evidence fetch was performed.

The fetched CMS publication page listed retrospective releases but did not verify an August 2026 publication date. The supplied resolutionDate, 2026-12-15, is preserved as ledger context and remains unverified. CMS specifications describe state submission deadlines, which do not establish a public release date.

The ledger does not explicitly identify the share denominator. CMS distinguishes renewals due, Metric 5, from total renewed, Metric 5a; ex parte renewals are Metric 5a1. The stopped run did not establish which denominator the registered share requires.

Prior/update/interval: No base rate, persistence prior, sigma, or 80% interval was finalized because the run stopped and the exact share denominator and official release date were not verified. Null estimates indicate failure, not numerical forecasts.
